candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite mixed numbers and whole numbers as equivalent improper fractions (or as fractions with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe converting mixed numbers to improper fractions and rewriting whole numbers as fractions (optionally with a chosen denominator) as a preparatory step for subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Each codebook includes selecting/deriving a shared denominator (commonly via LCM) and scaling numerators/denominators to form equivalent fractions before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are expressed in compatible forms (e.g., same denominator or separated whole and fractional parts), including recognizing zero results.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define the core subtraction operation after compatibility is established, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator or subtracting whole and fractional parts separately.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms and/or express an improper fraction as a mixed number or integer as the final reported form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include post-subtraction simplification (reducing to lowest terms) and final-form formatting (mixed number/integer) as a distinct concluding skill.

alignment_summary: Across A, B, and C, the skill sets align one-to-one into four shared concepts: (1) converting mixed/whole numbers to fraction form, (2) finding/using a common denominator via equivalent fractions, (3) performing the subtraction once forms are compatible (including zero results), and (4) simplifying and formatting the final answer. Every expert skill_id maps cleanly to exactly one of these four concepts, yielding 3/3 consensus for all.
